71bf82146cb3.old_english: WWOX-system, one preparation read in full and re-extracted (PMID 34634460, Table 1 and Figure 6): resting potential -79.25, -75.51, -73.62 mV and sag at a fixed -200 pA step 1.18, 2.04, 2.57 mV grade with gene dose, input resistance saturates at one allele, rebound is marked larger only in the knockout (the printed p cannot be reproduced from the Table 1 means and dispersion under stated assumptions), and bursts occur in 36 of 42 knockout, 4 of 23 heterozygote and 0 of 11 wild-type slices; the authors name control of the resting membrane potential as a factor underlying the hyperexcitability (the frequency-current slope does not differ once the curves are shifted to one step below rheobase; supplement not read) and cite discordant Ih-blocker precedents, including worsening of 4-AP events. Compound side: Ih-acting tools exist in the catalogue (a clinically used HCN blocker and several research blockers, identities resolved), found by the need search without naming any; their cellular potency in a cortical pyramidal neuron and their selectivity among HCN isoforms were not assessed here. No Ih-blocker experiment in a Wwox-deficient preparation is recorded in the entries read. [IT39] Ivabradine blocks sag and hyperpolarises cortical L5 and L6 neurons in normal rat slices, and injection into somatosensory cortex cut absence-seizure time by 96 percent against 40 percent in thalamic VB (abstract); the GAERS authors read Ih as not an adaptive response to spike-wave discharges (input resistance fell, resting potential and sag unchanged), which sits beside the discordant precedents.
71bf82146cb3.added_english: [IT40] A7 Tool notes: the research Ih blocker used in thalamic neurons (20 umol/L: about 17 mV hyperpolarisation, sag 0.4-2.1 mV left) is reported to block sodium and T-type current (abstract level for those papers); the Kv7 openers (a withdrawn antiseizure drug and a research compound) were read at abstract level only; K2P and Kir tool papers exist but none is shown to work in layer II/III pyramidal neurons.

83ef2e781b00.old_english: In knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: sag, resting potential, input resistance, rebound and burst incidence before and after two Ih blockers of different chemotypes (the second so that an off-target action is not read as Ih), with a current-clamp step that matches the resting potential and the peak potential, with a smaller cell or immature membrane listed as its own candidate beside branch D, and a voltage-clamp read of the blocker-sensitive current in a subset of cells; animals, not cells, are the replicates. Branch D adds the potassium-current arm: the potassium currents sensitive to a Kv7 blocker and to a Kir-channel blocker in voltage clamp, and input resistance read with synaptic transmission blocked. [IT36] A first-generation Ih blocker at 50 uM is about 40 times its sodium-current IC50 in DRG neurons (age not stated); read a second chemotype and the blocker-sensitive current in voltage clamp; nickel/Z944 and Kv7 arms separate.
83ef2e781b00.added_english: [IT40] A4 Report access resistance, bridge balance and capacitance by genotype; add a Ba2+- or Kv7-blocker-sensitive difference current with its zero-crossing against E_K (about -97 to -98 mV from the declared solutions; the recorded potentials need a junction correction of about -13 mV that 34634460 did not measure, which puts the estimated sag peaks about 16-21 mV below E_K, so the prediction applies to the voltage-clamp difference current, not to the sag peak).
